central_node: Indigenous Ecological Knowledge, Biomimicry, and Community Wildlife Care

key_details: Khasi and Jaintia communities guide young aerial roots across streams
Hollowed betel nut trunks serve as direction guides
Bridges grow stronger over 15–30 years as roots thicken
Natural biological process where touching plant tissues graft together
Self-healing living structure superior to rusting steel or cracking concrete
Endures extreme monsoon humidity and flooding
Assamese women organized into the 'Hargila Army' to save storks
Protected tall nesting trees from being cut down
Placed soft rescue nets under nests to catch falling chicks
Rescued and rehabilitated endangered Greater Adjutant Storks
real_world_examples: Hargila Army led by Dr. Purnima Devi Barman in Assam
